target.name: Defective CYP11A1 causes AICSR
target.description: Every steroid hormone begins with the same reaction: cleavage of the cholesterol side chain to pregnenolone by the mitochondrial enzyme CYP11A1, working with the ferredoxin reductase and ferredoxin partners that shuttle electrons from NADPH to the P450. When mutations disable this first committed step, no cortisol, aldosterone or sex steroids can be made, producing congenital adrenal insufficiency with 46,XY sex reversal.

target.name: catechol-containing compound catabolic process
target.description: catechol-containing compound catabolic process is the inactivation and clearance of catecholamines and related catechols, the chemistry that terminates dopamine, noradrenaline and adrenaline signalling and protects tissues from their reactive oxidation products. It sets how long a monoamine signal lasts at a synapse and how much of an ingested or circulating catechol survives first-pass metabolism, so its capacity shapes mood, movement, attention and blood pressure.

target.name: xenobiotic transmembrane transport
target.description: Cells must move drugs and other foreign chemicals across their membranes, and xenobiotic transmembrane transport is the combined import and export machinery that determines which compounds get in, how long they stay, and how they leave. It sets drug disposition in liver, kidney, intestine and the blood-brain barrier, and it is a common route to therapeutic failure: overexpression of the ATP-driven efflux pumps here confers multidrug resistance in tumours, while loss of hepatobiliary transporters such as ABCB11 or ABCC2 causes cholestasis and hyperbilirubinaemia.

target.name: aminoacyl-tRNA metabolism involved in translational fidelity
target.description: Accurate protein synthesis depends on each tRNA carrying the amino acid its anticodon specifies, and this proofreading arm of aminoacyl-tRNA metabolism is what keeps translational fidelity high. Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases for alanine, isoleucine, leucine, valine and threonine can misactivate near-isosteric amino acids, so they carry editing domains that hydrolyse mischarged products; separate trans-editing factors, including the D-aminoacyl-tRNA deacylases and free-standing synthetase-like domains, clear errors the synthetases themselves miss, notably D-amino acids wrongly attached to tRNA.

[untitled BTM module] A mixed immune-expression module centred on mononuclear leukocyte identity and trafficking, combining chemokine receptors, GTPase-of-immunity-associated proteins and transcriptional regulators. Loss or blockade of this axis limits atherosclerotic plaque myeloid influx and blunts inflammatory infiltration, which is why it is a longstanding drug target.
